title: Chemical Coordination and Integration

standard_code: Class 11 Biology, Chapter 19: Chemical Coordination and Integration
standard_text: Endocrine glands and hormones; human endocrine system – hypothalamus, pituitary, pineal, thyroid, parathyroid, adrenal, pancreas, gonads; mechanism of hormone action (elementary idea); role of hormones as messengers and regulators; hypo- and hyperactivity and related disorders.

key_big: Each endocrine gland releases hormones into the blood.

body_html:
How to think about it

Endocrine glands are ductless and release hormones into the blood. The hypothalamus controls the pituitary, which controls the thyroid, adrenal cortex and gonads. The thyroid makes thyroxine (metabolic rate) and calcitonin; the parathyroids raise blood Ca²⁺; the pancreas makes insulin and glucagon; the adrenal medulla makes adrenaline.

Protein hormones bind membrane receptors and use second messengers such as cAMP; steroid hormones enter the cell and act on genes. Lack of insulin causes diabetes mellitus, lack of iodine causes goitre, and too much growth hormone causes gigantism or acromegaly.

Example

Gland that makes insulin?

β-cells

Answer: pancreas

Example

Low iodine causes?

thyroid swells

Answer: goitre

Common mistakes

  • Calling insulin a steroid.
  • Saying the posterior pituitary makes oxytocin itself.
  • Mixing up gigantism and acromegaly.

faq.q: Why is the pituitary called the master gland?
faq.a: Its hormones control several other endocrine glands, though it is itself controlled by the hypothalamus.
They pass through the cell membrane and bind receptors inside the cell, changing which genes are expressed.

items.q: Which gland secretes oxytocin?
c: the posterior pituitary (made in the hypothalamus)
the Leydig cells of the testis
items.e: Oxytocin is made in the posterior pituitary (made in the hypothalamus).
